The AMoRE project is described as a series of experiments in three phases (Pilot, I, II); each phase has its own record, linked by lineage.
Planned schedule in the 2015 design report: AMoRE-Pilot 2015-2016 with 1.5 kg; the executed pilot ran 2015-2018 with 1.9 kg.

physics_goals.quote: The Advanced Molybdenum-based Rare process Experiment (AMoRE) aims to search for neutrinoless double beta decay (0$\nu\beta\beta$) of $^{100}$Mo with $\sim$100 kg of $^{100}$Mo-enriched molybdenum embedded in cryogenic detectors with a dual heat and light readout.
physics_goals.value: Search for neutrinoless double beta decay of 100Mo with ~100 kg of 100Mo-enriched molybdenum in cryogenic detectors; the pilot stage tests the technique and backgrounds

summary.plain: AMoRE-Pilot was the first, small stage of the AMoRE experiment: six calcium-molybdate crystals (1.9 kg) cooled to a few thousandths of a degree above absolute zero, run at the Yangyang laboratory from 2015 to 2018 to look for neutrinoless double beta decay of molybdenum-100. It found no such decay and set a limit.
summary.technical: Six 48depl-Ca100MoO4 crystals (1.9 kg total), phonon and scintillation readout with metallic magnetic calorimeters at mK temperatures (dilution refrigerator), in the A5 area of Y2L (700 m). First results from 111 kg d: T1/2(0vbb, 100Mo) > 9.5e22 yr (90% C.L.); a later background study sets T1/2 >= 3.0e23 yr.
